We’ll follow this flow: 1. **Quick syllabus map** → What’s in scope. 2. **Concept-by-concept teaching** → HTML → CSS basics → JavaScript (syntax, variables, data types, operators, control structures, loops, functions, arrays, objects, array methods). 3. **Debug-style practice questions** → Same format as your exam (like Q1–Q4). 4. **Mini-summary** after each major section to help you revise fast. --- ## **1. Syllabus Map from Exam Notice** You’re tested on: - **HTML & CSS basics** - Basic Tags, Lists, Tables - Forms & Input Elements + Form Validation - CSS Basic Selectors (element, class, id) - **JavaScript Basics** - Syntax, Variables, Data Types - Control Structures: `if`, `else`, `switch` - Loops: `for`, `while` - Functions & Scope, Closures - Objects, Arrays - Array Methods: `push`, `pop`, `map`, `filter` - **Debugging** — Fix broken HTML/JS and explain the corrections. --- ## **2. HTML Form Debugging** **Buggy code:** ```html Student Registration

Student Registration Form

Email:
Password:
``` **Fixed code:** ```html Student Registration

``` **Errors Fixed:** - `` → `` and `` - Mismatched heading tags (`

`) - `metod="psot"` → `method="post"` - `typ="text"` → `type="text"`, `type="emal"` → `type="email` - Spelling: `"passowrd"` → `"password"` - `"sumbit"` → `"submit"` - Added `required` for form validation (HTML5 best practice). **Expected Output:** A valid registration form that accepts user input and sends data to `google.com` when submitted. --- ### **Q2. HTML Text Formatting Debugging** **Buggy code:** ```html Bold and Italic Example

This is a bold word and this is an italic ``` **Fixed code:** ```html Bold and Italic Example

This is a bold word and this is an italic word.

``` **Errors Fixed:** - `` not closed properly. - `` closing tag missing before `word`. - HTML tags must be properly nested and closed. **Expected Output:** Displays: > This is a **bold** word and this is an *italic* word. --- ### **Q3. JS Array Reverse (Like your Q3)** **Buggy code:** ```js const a = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]; for (let i = 0; i <= Math.floor(a.length / 2); i++) { let temp = a[i]; a[i] = a[a.length - 1 - i]; a[a.length - 1 - i] = temp; } console.log(a); ``` **Fixed code:** ```js const a = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]; for (let i = 0; i < Math.floor(a.length / 2); i++) { let temp = a[i]; a[i] = a[a.length - 1 - i]; a[a.length - 1 - i] = temp; } console.log(a); ``` **Errors Fixed:** - Loop condition `<=` causes the middle element to swap with itself twice — unnecessary. - Changed to `< Math.floor(...)`. **Expected Output:** ``` [5, 4, 3, 2, 1] ``` --- ### **Q4. Function Debugging (Like your Q4)** **Buggy code:** ```js function calculateAverage(scores) { const sum = scores.reduce((acc, score) => acc + score); return sum / scores.length; } function determineWinner(team1Scores, team2Scores) { const team1Avg = calculateAverage(team1Scores); const team2Avg = calculateAverage(team2Scores); console.log(`Team 1 Average: ${team1Avg.toFixed(2)}`); console.log(`Team 2 Average: ${team2Avg.toFixed(2)}`); if (team1Avg >= team2Avg * 2) { console.log("Team 1 wins!"); } else if (team2Avg >= team1Avg * 2) { console.log("Team 2 wins!"); } else { console.log("No team wins based on the double average rule."); } } determineWinner([96, 108, 89], [250, 305, 400]); ``` **Fixed code:** ```js function calculateAverage(scores) { const sum = scores.reduce((acc, score) => acc + score, 0); // Added initial value 0 return sum / scores.length; } function determineWinner(team1Scores, team2Scores) { const team1Avg = calculateAverage(team1Scores); const team2Avg = calculateAverage(team2Scores); console.log(`Team 1 Average: ${team1Avg.toFixed(2)}`); console.log(`Team 2 Average: ${team2Avg.toFixed(2)}`); if (team1Avg >= team2Avg * 2) { console.log("Team 1 wins!"); } else if (team2Avg >= team1Avg * 2) { console.log("Team 2 wins!"); } else { console.log("No team wins based on the double average rule."); } } determineWinner([96, 108, 89], [250, 305, 400]); ``` **Errors Fixed:** - `.reduce()` needs an initial value (`0`) or first element becomes initial accumulator. - Without initial value, empty array will cause error. **Expected Output:** ``` Team 1 Average: 97.67 Team 2 Average: 318.33 Team 2 wins! ``` --- ### 🔥 **Why This Format Will Help You in CA1** - **Q1 & Q2** check **HTML correctness**. - **Q3** checks **logic in loops & arrays**. - **Q4** checks **functions, array methods, and conditional logic**. - These are exactly the 4 skill types your CA1 is built on. --- If you want, I can now **give you 10 extra rapid-fire debugging questions** (mixed HTML + JS) so you can do them tonight and be 100% exam-ready tomorrow.
